evidence: Full head-to-toe check at 07:25: no injury, no pain, observations normal. GP reviewed at 11:00 and found no injury. No treatment needed.
summary: E.W. caught her foot on a bath mat while walking to the bathroom with a care worker present as per her care plan and sat down on the floor. No injury, no pain, no treatment needed. Bath mat replaced with non-slip mat.

evidence: Staff called police at 15:30 and reported R.T. missing.
summary: R.T. left the unit through a contractor-propped garden gate. Police were called and found him 2 km away at a bus stop, cold and confused but unhurt. Gate now alarmed and contractor induction reviewed.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: M.K. said "he grabbed me hard last night when I didn't want to get up". One care worker assisted M.K. with a transfer at about 02:00.
summary: Staff found bruising on M.K.'s forearms after a care worker's overnight transfer. M.K. reported being grabbed hard. GP prescribed pain relief and dressings. Care worker stood down pending investigation.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: J.P.'s daughter reported four cash withdrawals totalling $240 from her father's bank card between 1 and 10 October. J.P. has not left the facility this month. The card is kept in the facility safe. The safe access log shows one staff member opened it on each of the four days.
summary: Resident's daughter reported four unauthorised cash withdrawals totalling $240 from resident's bank card kept in the facility safe. Safe access log shows one staff member opened the safe on each occasion. Staff member stood down and card cancelled.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: The night agency nurse raised both bed rails for D.L. overnight "to stop him wandering". D.L. has no assessment, consent or behaviour support plan for bed rails.
summary: Agency nurse raised both bed rails overnight to prevent wandering without assessment, consent, or behaviour support plan. Rails lowered at 06:00. No injury or distress.

evidence: A.N. requires minced and moist meals under her speech pathologist's plan. At lunch she was served a regular-texture roast.
summary: Resident requiring minced and moist meals was served a regular-texture roast. She coughed on the first mouthful. Staff removed the meal; RN assessed no distress or treatment needed. Minced meal served. Kitchen labelling under review.
